Observation: No visible focus indicator appears on links, buttons, or fields when navigating by keyboard; suppressed globally in the CSS reset.
Impact: Keyboard-only users cannot tell where they are on the page.
Recommendation: Restore visible focus states site-wide in the global stylesheet.
At a Glance: Patients who navigate by keyboard can't reliably tell where they are on any page of the site.
Evidence: https://carepath.example/, /book, /reset-password, /insurance-faq; global.css `*:focus { outline: none }`; tabbed through each page, no focus ring
Instances: 4 pages: Homepage, Appointment Booking, Password Reset, Insurance FAQ (shared stylesheet)

Location: Appointment Booking page, Confirm Appointment button
Observation: Confirm button is a styled div with a click handler; no accessible name or role.
Impact: Screen reader users hear nothing identifying the button's purpose.
At a Glance: Screen reader users can't tell what the booking submit button does.

Observation: Answer text is light gray on white at 3.2:1.
Impact: Low-vision users struggle to read answers.
Recommendation: Darken answer text to at least 4.5:1.
At a Glance: Some patients will find the FAQ answers hard to read.

Observation: Errors appear only as a generic 'Something went wrong' banner.
Impact: Users can't tell how to fix the problem.
At a Glance: Patients who mistype during password reset aren't told how to fix it.
Evidence: https://carepath.example/reset-password; submitted an unknown email and a mismatched password; both gave the same 'Something went wrong' banner

Observation: No loading state after submit; button can be clicked repeatedly.
Recommendation: Disable the button and show progress while submitting.
At a Glance: Patients aren't sure their booking went through.
Evidence: https://carepath.example/book step 3; pressed Submit twice quickly with requests blocked; button stayed active, no spinner

Observation: No way to go back to edit an earlier step without restarting.
Impact: Users abandon or restart the flow.
Recommendation: Add a Back control that preserves entered data.
At a Glance: Patients who make a mistake have to start their booking over.
Evidence: https://carepath.example/book step 3; no Back control; browser Back returned to the homepage

Observation: Answers use insurer jargon (e.g., 'coordination of benefits') without explanation.
Recommendation: Rewrite in plain language with definitions.
At a Glance: Insurance answers are written for insiders, not patients.

Impact: Mobile users can't reach key navigation.
Recommendation: Collapse nav into a menu below 768px.
At a Glance: On phones, patients can't reach parts of the main menu.
Evidence: https://carepath.example/ at 375 px (iPhone 13 emulation); header nav scrollWidth 612 px
Instances: 4 pages: Homepage, Appointment Booking, Password Reset, Insurance FAQ (shared header)
